Car park and hardstand cleaning in Melbourne

Large areas that cannot simply close

Retail car parks, office decks, hardstand and loading areas. The cleaning is straightforward and the areas are big, which makes the rate per square metre low. The problem is that people need to park on it while we are there, which is a logistics exercise before it is a cleaning one.

  • Sectioned so the site keeps operating
  • Overnight where the area can close
  • Rate falls as the area rises
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Commercial
  3. Car parks and hardstands

What is actually on a car park

Four things, in rough order of how much work each takes. Biological growth in the areas that stay shaded and damp, usually the perimeter and under any cover. Rubber deposit where cars turn and brake, which is plasticiser migrating into the surface rather than dirt. Oil, in the bays where vehicles sit. And general traffic film across the whole thing.

Only the first comes off with water. The other three need degreasing and chemistry, which is why a car park that was simply pressure washed looks better and still has every oil patch and tyre mark on it.

Keeping it open

The ways it can be run, and what each one suits

How a car park job is normally scheduled, with the honest cost implication.
  How it works Cost effect
Fully closed, overnight The whole area in one go with nothing to work around Cheapest per square metre by a clear margin
Sectioned, during trading Quarter or half at a time, bays coned off and rotated Longer, so it costs more. Often the only option for retail
By level, over nights One deck per night on a multi level car park Middle. Predictable and easy to communicate to tenants
Weekend, partial closure Office and industrial sites where weekends are genuinely quiet Close to the overnight rate without the night loading
Spot treatment only Oil patches and entry areas rather than the whole surface Cheapest absolutely, but it leaves the deck looking patchy

Swipe for the rest of the columns

Worth knowing

Three things that come up every time

Cleaning restores more line marking than people expect

A lot of marking that looks faded is actually dirty. On a car park that was due for remarking, cleaning first often changes the brief and saves the line marking budget.

Where the water goes matters

A car park drains to stormwater by design. Run off carrying degreaser and hydrocarbon is managed and directed rather than released, and on some sites that is a licence condition rather than good practice.

Asphalt is not concrete

Asphalt softens with heat and some degreasers attack the binder. It is cleaned at lower pressure with different chemistry, and anyone treating it like a concrete slab will damage it.

Questions

From centre and facilities managers

Can you clean our car park without closing it?

Yes, by working it in sections with bays coned off and rotated. It takes longer than closing the area would, so it costs more, and for most retail sites it is the right trade.

Where a site can genuinely close overnight, that is faster and cheaper and we will show you the difference in the quote.

How is a large area priced?

Per square metre, with the rate falling as the area rises, and condition on top. Scheduling then moves it: a closed site is cheaper than a sectioned one.

A first clean on a car park that has been left for years is priced separately from the ongoing cycle, because it is a catch up rather than a maintenance visit.

Will cleaning remove the oil stains?

Substantially. Degreasing lifts what is on the surface and a poultice draws back what has soaked in. On a bay where a vehicle has leaked for years, the realistic outcome is a major improvement rather than invisibility.

Oil stain removal covers how that works.

Can you clean asphalt as well as concrete?

Yes, carefully and differently. Asphalt softens in heat and some degreasers attack the bitumen binder, so it is cleaned at lower pressure with chemistry chosen for it.

Treating asphalt like a concrete slab is how a car park ends up with scoured patches.

What about the stormwater drains?

Run off is managed and directed away from stormwater entries, and solids are collected. Where your site has specific conditions in a licence or a trade waste agreement, those go into the method before the price rather than after.

How often should a car park be cleaned?

Twice a year for a retail car park, annually for an office or industrial one, and more often where there are trees dropping onto it.

The frequency that is cheapest overall is the one that never lets growth and oil build into a restoration job.
